notes: The course: lessons from easy to hard. Each playable lesson is a scene (a generated level or your garage), the route the coach teaches, the words for it and a rule for passing.

route.start is the rear-axle pose [x, z, heading in radians]; route.pieces are [direction, steering, metres]: direction 1 forward, -1 reverse; steering -1 full lock left, 0 straight, 1 full lock right. They are stored, not planned on the phone, so every device coaches the same route. test/lessons.test.ts checks that the planner (steering full lock or straight) still finds exactly these routes.

Every claim in explain and tips comes from docs/research/parking-tips.md and lists its sources; where sources disagree, the text says so. tips are keyed by step number and shown with that step's mark.

scene.kerbGap: in a space along a kerb, the route was planned to finish with the body this far from the kerb (the template also allows 0.2 m); 0.15 puts the tyres about 17 cm out, in the middle of the 30 cm the pass allows.

scene.build: a scene made for a lesson (core/generator/lessonScenes.ts): first-metres, turning, leaving (a kerb level with the car parked and an exit lane), angled (60° bays). route.authored: written for the lesson rather than found by the planner (the cone course, the U-turn, the one-turn angled entry); the test checks it clears everything and passes.

pass: angle (degrees off straight), centre (metres off centre), kerb (tyres to the kerb, metres), moves ('par+1'), face ('in' or 'out'). Nothing touched is always required, and so is finishing in the target (a bay, or for leaving, the lane ahead).

tow: a towing lesson, always in the car with a tow bar (the Octavia) with this trailer; scene.tow is one of the trailer yards (core/generator/towScenes.ts), each with the path the trailer's axle follows. The coach steers by that path (core/towing.ts): no stored route. chapter: a heading in the course list before this lesson.

lessons.title: First metres
lessons.learn: Forward, reverse, stopping and steering, round a cone course.

explain.text: Hold Forward or Reverse to move: a short press creeps at about 4 km/h, and the car stops when you let go. In lessons the coach keeps you at walking pace, as driving schools put it.
Reverse slowly, check all your mirrors and blind spots, and look mainly through the rear window.

The coach has you set the wheel while the car is stopped. Sources disagree about this dry steering: DVSA says it wears the tyres and steering, the driving test does not mark it as a fault, and Bill Plant and Oregon teach it.
The course: forward to the stop line, back to the blue cone, then round on full lock into the green bay.

1.text: Let go a little before the line: the car takes a moment to stop.

2.text: Highway Code: reverse slowly, and look mainly through the rear window.

lessons.title: How a car turns
lessons.learn: The rear wheels cut inside and the front swings out: your turning circle.

explain.text: On full lock your {car} turns in a circle {circle}. The dashed lines on the floor are the path it sweeps on full lock: the inner one is where your inner rear wheel runs, the outer one where your outer front corner swings.
The front of the car swings out as you turn.
Handbooks for lorries and buses warn that the rear wheels cut in towards the kerb. A car does the same, by less: on the plan, the thin cyan line shows where your inner rear wheel will run.
When you reverse, the steered wheels are effectively at the back, so the front swings the other way.

2.text: Keep the wheel on full lock all the way round: the inner cone passes your rear wheel, the outer cones pass your front corner.

lessons.title: Into a bay, forwards
lessons.learn: Turn when your mirror reaches the bay's near line.

explain.text: Handbooks that teach parking forwards use the mirror: from 1.5–2.4 m (5–8 ft) out, turn when your mirror reaches the target bay's own near line, not two bays before.
Here the bay is {bay} m wide with no cars beside it, so you can watch the rule work. The coach stops you at each mark: set the wheel, then drive on.

1.text: Georgia and Montana: turn when your mirror reaches the bay's near line.

cue.mark: the near line of the green bay

lessons.title: Between two cars
lessons.learn: The same turn with a car on each side and a narrower aisle.

explain.text: The same rule as the last lesson: turn when your mirror reaches the bay's near line. The bay is {bay} m wide and the cars either side are parked off centre, so the mark matters more.
The front of your car swings out as you turn.
Going forwards, your inner rear wheel cuts inside the front ones: the thin cyan line on the plan shows where it runs. Keep it clear of the car in the near bay.

1.text: Georgia and Montana: turn when your mirror reaches the bay's near line.

cue.mark: the near line of the green bay

lessons.title: Reverse into a bay
lessons.learn: Full lock when the bay's line is level with your back seat; straighten when the lines look parallel.

explain.text: Why reverse in: Montana calls it far less risky, you drive out forwards instead of reversing out half-blind, and the Highway Code recommends it for driveways (rule 201). Sources disagree for car parks: German multi-storeys often want you nose in.

UK driving schools: drive past and stop about two car lengths past the bay. Turn to full lock when the bay's first line is level with your back seat, seen in the rear passenger window; other schools use the door handle or the rear door. Straighten when the lines look parallel in both mirrors.

1.text: UK schools: stop about two car lengths past the bay, then full lock as the bay's first line meets your back seat.

2.text: Straighten when the bay's lines look parallel in both mirrors.

lessons.title: Parallel, big space
lessons.learn: Line up, full lock towards the kerb, then full lock away at the mirror cue.

explain.text: This space is about 1.5 car lengths, the size handbooks suggest for beginners.
Line up: stop about 0.6–1 m (2–3 ft) out from the car in front, with your rear bumper level with its rear bumper or a little ahead.
Reverse with the wheel turned towards the kerb. Sources disagree on how far: US handbooks say full or sharp lock, UK schools teach one turn of the wheel. This route uses full lock.

Georgia: when your mirror is in line with the front car's rear bumper, steer quickly the other way (Montana says the kerb-side mirror). Most other sources wait until the front of your car is clear of the car in front.
Finish within 30 cm (1 ft) of the kerb.

1.text: Line up about 0.6–1 m out, your rear bumper level with the front car's or a little ahead.

cue.mark: the back of the car in front

2.text: Georgia: steer the other way when your mirror is in line with the front car's rear bumper.

3.text: Within 30 cm (1 ft) of the kerb.

lessons.title: Parallel, tighter
lessons.learn: The three-phase way: straighten at about 45°, reverse straight, then full lock away.

explain.text: A tighter space: your car's length plus 1.8 m. California's smallest is the car's length plus 3 ft (0.9 m).
Three-phase methods straighten the wheels at about 45°: when your centre door pillar or front door reaches the front car's rear bumper, or when your bonnet points to 2 o'clock.

Then reverse straight back and steer away once the front of your car is clear of the car in front; this route uses full lock. New York instead says when your front wheels are opposite its back bumper.
One correction move is allowed: par plus one.

1.text: Line up about 0.6–1 m out, your rear bumper level with the front car's or a little ahead.

cue.mark: the back of the car in front

2.text: About 45°: your door pillar reaches the front car's rear bumper, or your bonnet points to 2 o'clock.

3.text: DVSA: steer away once you are sure the front of your car is clear of the parked car.

4.text: Within 30 cm (1 ft) of the kerb.

lessons.title: Leaving a tight space
lessons.learn: Back up to the car behind, wheels away from the kerb, then out without touching.

explain.text: You start parked with your nose 35 cm from the car in front. Back up to the car behind. Turn the wheels away from the kerb, signal and check over both shoulders before you move off.
Creep out while steering, and straighten when your front seat passes the car ahead's bumper.
On this route you back up with the wheel turned towards the kerb, which angles your nose out of the space, then pull out on full lock the other way.

1.text: New York: back up to the car behind, then turn the wheels away from the kerb.

2.text: Georgia: creep out while steering, and straighten when your front seat passes the car ahead's bumper.

cue.mark: the back of the car in front

lessons.title: Angled bays
lessons.learn: Turn sharply as your steering wheel passes the first line.

explain.text: Georgia: approach about 1–1.2 m (3–4 ft) out from the parked cars, and turn sharply as your steering wheel passes the first line of the bay.
These bays are at 60° to the aisle, so the turn is two thirds of a right angle: one full-lock turn, then straight in.

1.text: Georgia: turn sharply as your steering wheel passes the first line.

cue.mark: the near line of the green bay

lessons.title: Your garage
lessons.learn: Everything at once: bay 561, nose in, from the left.

explain.text: Your own bay, nose in, coming from the left as you usually do. The Peugeot 208 narrows the end of the aisle, so the route takes three moves: turn in on full lock, back up on full lock the other way, then drive straight in.
Mind pillar 560 on the left of the bay and the concrete bench at its head.
If you can't see in the real garage, get someone to guide you.

lessons.title: Reversing a trailer straight
lessons.learn: Keep a trailer straight as you back it 13 m into a space.

explain.text: Pushed backwards, a trailer goes the opposite way to the car: turn the car's wheels to the right and the trailer goes left. The other way to think of it: put your hand at the bottom of the steering wheel, and the trailer goes the way your hand moves.

Back slowly, so there is time to correct, and correct as soon as the trailer starts to drift. Sharp corrections make the trailer jackknife, which can damage the back of the car and the front of the trailer.

This trailer is short, about 2.3 m from the ball to its axle (an estimate: its maker does not give it), so a small angle grows quickly. Here it starts 3° off. With a trailer on, holding Reverse creeps at 0.5 m/s, and the car's rear parking sensors are off.
If the trailer gets away from you, stop and pull forward to straighten it, then try again.
In a guided try a yellow mark on the wheel's rim shows where to hold it: keep your hand on the wheel and follow the mark.

lessons.title: Reversing round a corner
lessons.learn: Back the trailer round a corner into a side lane, and into the space at its end.

explain.text: To send the back of the trailer one way, turn the car's front wheels the other way. Then the car has to follow the trailer round, or the rig keeps folding until it jackknifes: round a right angle, the car's path is an S.
So: steer to start the trailer turning, steer back to follow it round the corner, and straighten as it lines up with the lane.

Oregon's manual says it the other way round: when the trailer drifts off its line, turn the top of the steering wheel towards the drift. That moves your hand at the bottom of the wheel the other way, the way you want the trailer to go.
The corner is on your left, the driver's side, so you can watch the trailer through your own window as well as in the mirrors.

lessons.title: Reversing into a space
lessons.learn: Back the trailer into a space between two parked cars.

explain.text: Ontario's truck handbook: back in from the driver's side, set up with the trailer angled the way you want it to go, and back slowly, watching the trailer through your window and in the mirrors.
If the trailer turns too early or too sharply, ease the steering off; if it turns too late or too wide, steer more.
Here you start past the space with the trailer straight behind the car: the first metres of reversing angle it towards the space.
If it goes wrong, pull forward to straighten up and start again: Oregon's manual calls these pull-ups.
